content.comment_body: Hello, I need to connect my [product_name] to the [product_name] App through my router and the internet. My device has a fixed address like 192.168.1.13. The router uses DHCP; I reserved a static address for the device. I created a NAT rule in the router: internal port 8080, external port 8080, protocol TCP and UDP. I have a DNS server that converts my dynamic router address into a static address such as "[user_name].dyndns.fr". In the app's edit connection page, I set: Name: [user_name], IP Address/Hostname: [user_name].dyndns.fr, Port: 8080. It doesn’t work and I get errors trying to connect the app. Can anyone help?
Do a lookup to see which IP address you get from your dynamic DNS. I think the issue may be with how the app handles host lookup.

I only have the domain name from dynamic DNS, like [user_name].dyndns.fr, not the actual IP address. In the app, I configured: Name: PC-7 (the DHCP name for the device), IP Address/Hostname: [user_name].dyndns.fr.
On your computer, use nslookup or install the PingTools app from Google Play to do a DNS lookup there. With your dynamic DNS settings, you should find the IP address.

When I use nslookup on my PC, the default server is livebox.home, address 192.168.1.1. When I perform a DNS lookup on my phone using PingTools and enter my domain name, I receive my router’s address. Does this mean it is configured correctly?

This seems incorrect. If you use nslookup with your dynamic DNS address such as [user_name].dyndns.fr, it should return your internet router’s external address, not 192.168... (which is internal and not reachable over the internet). If you send me your real dynamic DNS address in a private message, I can check it for you.

analysis.insight_summary: The user encounters issues connecting their [product_name] device to the [product_name] App remotely via the internet, despite configuring NAT and using a dynamic DNS domain name. There’s confusion around DNS resolution, particularly regarding how the app interprets hostnames and returns addresses, highlighting a lack of clarity and feedback in network setup and DNS handling within the application.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates effortless remote access to their [product_name] device using a custom domain from dynamic DNS, following NAT forwarding setup. They expect to control and access the device through the [product_name] App with their DDNS hostname over the internet.
